item.title: gnustep-base: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA file
item.description:
Part of #576541.

gnustep-base has a bundled CA file, GSTLS/ca-certificates.crt, in the resource bundle of the library, in the lib output. When the GSTLSCAFile user default, GS_TLS_CA_FILE and SSL_CERT_FILE are not set, GSTLS gives this file to GnuTLS as the default CA file. GSTLS uses the file when it checks the certificate of a server. By default, GNUstep does not check server certificates, thus to use the file, an application must set GSTLSVerifyServer, GS_TLS_VERIFY_S or the GSTLSVerify option of a request. This change replaces the file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert in postInstall.

[!NOTE] AI Disclosure: Claude Code made the code change, the commit message and the first version of this pull request description, with patchix. Claude Code used Claude Opus 5.5. item.title: kodi: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA bundle
item.description:
Part of #576541.

Kodi installs a bundled CA file, share/kodi/system/certs/cacert.pem, from system/certs/cacert.pem of the source. The file has 143 certificates. 23 of these certificates are not in cacert. 12 certificates are in cacert, but they are not TLS roots of cacert. 10 TLS roots of cacert are not in the file. The file has the root emSign ECC Root CA - G3. On Windows, Android, darwin and webOS, Kodi sets SSL_CERT_FILE to this file. On Linux, Kodi reads the file only when catrustfile in advancedsettings.xml or an add-on points to it. This change replaces the file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert, in postInstall of unwrapped.nix.

item.title: renpy: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA file
item.description:
Part of #576541.

Ren'Py has a bundled CA file, share/renpy/lib/python3.12/certifi/cacert.pem, from the upstream SDK. This file is part of the Python interpreter of the SDK, share/renpy/lib/py3-linux-x86_64/python. The launcher of Ren'Py copies this interpreter and the CA file into each game archive that it makes with Build Distributions. In the game from such an archive, renpy.fetch() and the updater use requests, and requests uses this file. bin/renpy does not use the file, because it uses the Python and the certifi package of nixpkgs. This change replaces the file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert in preFixup. The launcher copies the contents of the cacert file into the game archive, not the symlink. A line above the change gives the upstream report https://github.com/renpy/renpy/issues/7466. When upstream closes this report, a person can remove the change.

item.title: flyspray: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA bundle
item.description:
Part of #576541.

Flyspray installs a copy of the Guzzle 3 PHP library. This library has a bundled CA file, vendor/guzzle/guzzle/src/Guzzle/Http/Resources/cacert.pem. The file has 153 certificates. 116 of these certificates are not in cacert. The file does not have 97 TLS roots of cacert. The harness finds 132 roots in the file that are not TLS roots of cacert. item.title: cudatext: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA bundle
item.description:
Part of #576541.

CudaText has bundled copies of requests, urllib3 and certifi in share/cudatext/py/sys/. The cuda_addonman package of CudaText uses requests.get to get the files of extensions. By default, verify_https is True, and requests examines the server certificate with the bundled file, share/cudatext/py/sys/certifi/cacert.pem. The harness output shows that this file has 143 certificates. cacert does not accept 30 of these CAs for TLS, and 5 TLS roots of cacert are not in the file. The bundled file has the root emSign ECC Root CA - G3. This change replaces the bundled file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert in postFixup. item.title: nixos/ca: set NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE
item.description:
Right now, nss-cacert updates need to go though staging and changes to security.pki.caCertificateBlacklist (like in #576390 or like custom user preferences) are not directly picked up by applications using the cacert package.

This environment variable is patched-in in packages like pythons certifi to override the ca bundle at runtime.

Without this change certifi still uses an old version of the ca bundle:

❯ nix-shell -p python3Packages.certifi --command 'diff -u $(python -m certifi) /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt'
--- /nix/store/6x3vic5vm4jzp29yna1qkp0xmf3qm35i-nss-cacert-3.126/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt    1970-01-01 01:00:01.000000000 +0100
+++ /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt        1970-01-01 01:00:01.000000000 +0100
@@ -1758,8 +1758,15 @@

 Comodo AAA Services root
 Traditional PEM block omitted: this certificate is not trusted for authenticating servers.
-Trusted for:
+Rejected for:
+  - 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1 (RFC5280: serverAuth key usage)
+  - 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2 (RFC5280: clientAuth key usage)
+  - 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3 (RFC5280: codeSigning key usage)
   - 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.4 (RFC5280: emailProtection key usage)
+  - 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.8 (RFC5280: timeStamping key usage)
+  - 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.5 (RFC2459: ipsecEndSystem key usage)

item.title: pur: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA bundle
item.description:
Part of #576541.

pur bundles a copy of pip 23.2.1 in pur/packages. That copy has certifi 2023.5.7, with the file pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem. pur puts pur/packages first in sys.path. Thus the bundled requests reads this file for all HTTPS connections. The file has 141 certificates. 24 of them are not in cacert, and 18 are in cacert but not for TLS. The file contains the roots AAA Certificate Services and emSign ECC Root CA - G3. This change replaces the file with a symlink to ${cacert}/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt in postInstall. The rm command stops the build when a new version moves the file.

[!NOTE] AI Disclosure: Claude Code made the code change, the commit message and the first version of this pull request description, through patchix. Claude Code used Claude Opus 5.5. A person examined the work before this pull request. This pull request description is written in ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), examined with memelint in strict mode.

Test

nix-cacert-harness examines the package before and after this change. A local copy of nixpkgs is not necessary.

Output of harness: pur

base (before) = dac5e22db3ed2be013da0eba8050c05140bd3f30

==================================================================

before: dac5e22db3ed2be013da0eba8050c05140bd3f30   after: worktree <worktree>
before ok (0 built, 1s)
        drv /nix/store/sjf52dlkjzjqqhpjh8z5mdjc2g51wy6c-pur-7.4.0.drv
after  ok (0 built, 1s)
        drv /nix/store/zg88gbgkjsf13w04acvn35qwx4hszh2c-pur-7.4.0.drv

| output:path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| out:/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem | pem 141 certs: 24 not in cacert, 18 in cacert but not for TLS, 19 cacert TLS roots missing; scanner: AAA,ECC G3 | symlink->cacert:ca-bundle.crt pem 169 certs (118 TLS roots + 51 non-TLS, i.e. cacert's own trust-rules bundle) |

inside archives (scanner only; a symlink in the installed output cannot reach them, issue #576542 class):

  after  dist:/pur-7.4.0-py3-none-any.whl!pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem  roots=136 trusts AAA Certificate Services,emSign ECC Root CA - C3,emSign ECC Root CA - G3,emSign Root CA - C1,emSign Root CA - G1

cacert in runtime closure (before): no

  - C=IN, OU=emSign PKI, O=eMudhra Technologies Limited, CN=emSign ECC Root CA - G3
  - C=US, OU=emSign PKI, O=eMudhra Inc, CN=emSign ECC Root CA - C3
  - C=US, OU=emSign PKI, O=eMudhra Inc, CN=emSign Root CA - C1
  - C=AT, O=e-commerce monitoring GmbH, CN=GLOBALTRUST 2020
  - C=BE, O=GlobalSign nv-sa, OU=Root CA, CN=GlobalSign Root CA
  - C=BM, O=QuoVadis Limited, CN=QuoVadis Root CA 2
  - C=BM, O=QuoVadis Limited, CN=QuoVadis Root CA 3
  - C=CH, O=SwissSign AG, CN=SwissSign Gold CA - G2
  - C=CH, O=SwissSign AG, CN=SwissSign Silver CA - G2
VERDICT pur: FIXED: before trusted CAs outside cacert; after: 1 store(s) == cacert, none with extra CAs (+ bundles inside archives remain, see above)

eMudhra chains (--emudhra; offline and reproducible): the 14 chains in fixtures/emudhra,
each leaf verified against each store (openssl verify -purpose sslserver, at 2026-10-23):
| output:path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| out:/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem | pem: accepted 14/14 (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2) | symlink->cacert:ca-bundle.crt pem: accepted 0/14 |
inside archives (zip members, extracted):
| dist:/pur-7.4.0-py3-none-any.whl!pur/packages/pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem | pem: accepted 14/14 (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2) | pem: accepted 14/14 (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2) |
VERDICT pur emudhra: FIXED: before accepted 14/14 compromised eMudhra chains (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2); after 0/14 (+ after-side archive members accept 14/14 (g3: 7/7, aaa: 7/7, noct: 2/2), see table)

[2/2] live eMudhra test hosts: needs network, NOT reproducible offline
(no shims/pur.{nix,sh} or shims/live/pur.{nix,sh}: live check skipped)

Before the change, the bundled file accepts 14 of the 14 eMudhra chains. It accepts 7 of 7 for emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and 7 of 7 for AAA Certificate Services. After the change, the file is a symlink to the cacert bundle, and it accepts none of the 14 chains. The harness did not do the live test, because it has no shim for pur. item.title: linux: patch skb_zerocopy() to propagate the shared-frag marker
item.description:
The kernel just had several vulnerabilities accidentally posted to the public mailing list. Most of them can be mitigated by blacklisting kernel modules or blocking their autoload, except ZDI-CAN-33367, the network code local privilege escalation. The patches have not yet landed in a kernel release; this PR adds the most critical one.

[!NOTE] AI Disclosure: Claude Code made the code change, the commit message and the first version of this pull request description. Claude Code used Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5. I examined all of this work. This pull request description is written in ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), examined with memelint in strict mode.

This change adds the upstream patch net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_zerocopy() to the Linux kernels of nixpkgs. skb_zerocopy() copies the frags of one skb into a different skb, but it does not copy the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag. Thus, ESP input does not identify these frags as shared frags, and it writes the decrypted data into the same frags. Through nfnetlink_queue or an openvswitch upcall, an unprivileged user can write into the page cache of a read-only file that only root can change. The patch is on the netdev list with Cc: stable, but no kernel release has it at this time. This change adds the patch to linux_6_1, linux_6_6, linux_6_12, linux_6_18, linux_7_2, linux_7_3, linux_zen, linux_xanmod, linux_xanmod_stable and linux_xanmod_latest. For linux_7_3, fetchpatch gets the upstream patch. The other kernels do not have the from->unreadable check after the loop that copies the frags. Thus, they get skb-zerocopy-shared-frag-pre-7.3.patch, which has the same change, but the lines around it are different. linux_7_3 builds correctly on x86_64-linux.

Test

linux_7_3 builds correctly on x86_64-linux, and the patch applies without fuzz. I also applied the pre-7.3 patch with patch -p1 --dry-run to net/core/skbuff.c of each of the other kernels. The patch applies without fuzz to each kernel:

  • linux_6_1 (6.1.190): offset -507 lines
  • linux_6_6 (6.6.160): offset -234 lines
  • linux_6_12 (6.12.114): offset -12 lines
  • linux_6_18 (6.18.58): no offset
  • linux_7_2 (7.2.12): offset 51 lines
  • linux_zen (7.2.11-zen1): offset 51 lines
  • linux_xanmod (6.18.58-xanmod1): no offset
  • linux_xanmod_stable and linux_xanmod_latest (7.2.12-xanmod1): offset 51 lines
